title: Score references in Rust + wasm, saveScore as plan + shell (split from T23a)
description:
Goal: `saveScore` implements features/data/domain/score_refs.feature correctly, with the resolution logic in Rust (shared later with the engine's save_score, T13) and unit tests that exercise the real code. Split out of apricitus-0a00f3 (T23a), whose domain.ts saveScore resolved clips by the alias instead of the path, lost clipPath for unresolved refs, and collided on re-save.

Design: design/storage.md §1 (Score, ScoreRef; id rule `sref_<scoreId>_<alias>[_n]`), §5 step 5.

## 1. Rust: `apricitus_data::score_refs` (new module in crates/apricitus-data)

`pub fn catalog_refs(text: &str, folder: &str, file: &str) -> Result<Vec<CatalogRef>, Vec<String>>`
- Parse with `apricitus_score::parse_score(text, Path::new(&format!("{folder}/{file}")))`; parse errors are returned as `Err(messages)`.
- Call `apricitus_score::references`, then map each `Ref` to
  `CatalogRef { id_suffix, alias, source, catalog_path: Option<String>, clip_id: Option<String>, slice_name: Option<String>, slice_id: Option<String>, kit_pad: Option<String> }`.
- **The catalog-path rule (library mode):**
  - (a) `source` starts with `@clp_` → `clip_id = source[1..]`, `catalog_path = None`.
  - (b) The score has **no** `samples` directive → the source is already catalog-relative: `catalog_path = normalize(source)`.
  - (c) The score has `samples <dir>` → resolve `normalize(folder/dir/source)`, as if the repo root held `samples/` (the catalog). If the result starts with `samples/`, strip that prefix and use it. Otherwise, use the normalized path unchanged (it will stay unresolved). Example: folder `examples`, `samples ../samples`, source `marine-band/x.wav` → `marine-band/x.wav`.
  - Normalizing never produces a leading `./`; `..` that escapes the root stays as `..`.
- **Slices:**
  - A slice given as `@slc_…` → `slice_id = that[1..]`, `slice_name = None`.
  - Otherwise `slice_name` is the slice.
- **Deterministic order and ids:**
  - Sort by (alias, kit_pad, slice_name, source).
  - The base suffix is `alias`, plus `_<kit_pad>` when set.
  - A repeated suffix gets `_2`, `_3` and so on, in sorted order.
  - `id_suffix` is the final suffix; the TS layer builds `sref_<scoreId>_<id_suffix>`.
- **Unit tests in the module:**
  - rule (a), (b), (c) and the escape case;
  - the kit-pad scenario from score_refs.feature (2 refs, distinct suffixes);
  - duplicate numbering;
  - a parse error;
  - the same input twice gives an identical output.

## 2. wasm: `rw_references` wraps it
- Input `{text, folder, file}`; output `{data: [CatalogRef as camelCase JSON], errors: []}` or `{errors: [...]}`.
- Replace the three loose tests in web/test/wasm.test.mjs with **exact** `assert.deepEqual` on the whole `data` array for (i) the score_refs.feature scenario-1 text, (ii) the kit-pad scenario text, (iii) an `@clp_`/`@slc_` score, and (iv) a `samples ../samples` score in folder `examples`. Add one parse-error case.
- Fix `extractReferences` in web/src/apricitus.ts (it currently sends `base_dir`, which the export ignores) to send `{text, folder, file}` and to be typed with the new shape.

## 3. TS: pure plan plus a thin shell (web/src/data/plans.ts, new)
`planScoreRefs(scoreId, refs: CatalogRef[], lookups, existing: ScoreRef[]) -> {create: ScoreRef[], update: ScoreRef[], delete: string[]}`.
- `lookups` holds the resolved Clip for each catalog_path/clip_id and the Slice for each (clipId, name)/slice_id, already fetched by the shell.
- Record fields:
  - `id`, `scoreId`, `clipAlias = alias`;
  - `clipPath = catalog_path` (set **even when unresolved**, scenario 4) or the clip's path for id refs;
  - `clipId` if resolved, otherwise the field is **absent**;
  - `sliceName`, `sliceId`, `start`, `end` from the resolved slice;
  - never `owner` (the backend sets it).
- The diff against `existing` by id:
  - ids that are gone → `delete`;
  - same id → `update` with **every** field listed, and `null` for fields that are now absent, so a stale clipId or sliceId is cleared;
  - new ids → `create`.

`saveScore(scoreId, text)` in domain.ts becomes:
1. `Score.get`, then create (`title = scoreId`, `folder = "scores"`, `format = "apr"`) or update `text`.
2. `extractReferences(text, folder, scoreId + ".apr")`.
3. **On parse errors:** update `lastErrors` with the messages, leave the ScoreRefs untouched, and return `{data: score}`. A draft with errors still saves. **On success:** `lastErrors: []`.
4. Fetch the lookups:
   - `Clip.clipsByPath({path})` collecting **all** pages (`collectAll`), taking the first; `Clip.get` for id refs;
   - `Slice.slicesByClipAndName` for named slices; `Slice.get` for id slices.
5. Fetch the existing refs with `ScoreRef.refsByScore({scoreId})` (all pages), not `list` with a filter.
6. `planScoreRefs`.
7. Apply: deletes first, then updates, then creates. Return the first error, if any.

## 4. Tests
- **Delete web/test/data/domain.test.ts.** It never imports domain.ts; it tests its own fake.
- Add web/test/data/plans.test.ts. It imports `planScoreRefs` from src/data/plans.ts and uses `CatalogRef` inputs taken from **real wasm output** (load the built wasm the way wasm.test.mjs does) for the four score_refs.feature scenario texts. Assert the exact create/update/delete sets, including:
  - re-save replaces clp-1 with clp-2 (1 delete, 1 create, or an update with the old fields nulled);
  - unresolved: `clipPath: "somewhere/else.wav"` with no clipId;
  - saving the same text twice: an empty create and delete, updates only.

## Files you may touch
- crates/apricitus-data/src/{lib.rs,score_refs.rs};
- crates/apricitus-web/src/lib.rs (rw_references only);
- web/src/apricitus.ts (extractReferences only);
- web/src/data/{plans.ts,domain.ts (saveScore and helpers only)};
- web/test/wasm.test.mjs;
- web/test/data/{plans.test.ts, domain.test.ts (delete)}.

Nothing in web/src/ui or web/src/style.css.

## Verification (paste all outputs)
```
export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH
cargo test -p apricitus-data
cd web && npm run wasm && node test/wasm.test.mjs && npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsx --test test/data/*.test.ts && npm run build
```

comments.text:
Review round 1 (storage-lead): **sent back. The logic is close; the tests don't yet pin it.** Re-run by me: `cargo test -p apricitus-data` ✓, wasm ✓, tsc ✓, `tsx --test` 15/15 ✓.

Good: the catalog-path rules (a)/(b)/(c), `refsByScore` with collectAll, `clipPath` set for unresolved refs, deletes → updates → creates, and parse errors leaving refs untouched.

Fix these:

1. **Exact assertions (the spec's §2 and §4, not done).**
   - web/test/wasm.test.mjs still uses `.find` plus single fields. Replace the rw_references tests with `assert.deepEqual(result, {data: [...], errors: []})` on the whole output for:
     - (i) score_refs.feature scenario 1;
     - (ii) the kit-pad scenario (both refs, in order);
     - (iii) `@clp_`/`@slc_`;
     - (iv) a `samples ../samples` score in folder `examples`;
     - (v) a parse error: deepEqual on the `errors` array shape, i.e. a non-empty array of strings, and no `data` key.
   - web/test/data/plans.test.ts: `assert.deepEqual(plan, {create: [...], update: [...], delete: [...]})` on the whole plan in every test. Remove `refs.length > 0`, `.find`, `delete.length > 0` and the either/or branch in Scenario 7. The expected plan is determinate: the same id `sref_score-1_beat` → one update with `clipId: "clp-2"`, the new `clipPath`, and `sliceName/sliceId/start/end: null`.
   - Rust `test_kit_pad_references`: `assert_eq!` on the whole `Vec<CatalogRef>`.
2. **`test_duplicate_numbering` doesn't test duplicates.** `beat` and `beat2` are different suffixes. Build a real collision: a chopped kit gives the suffix `<alias>_<kit>`, so `clip brk = …`, `kit b = chop brk by beats 0.5`, plus a clip named `brk_b` collide on `brk_b`. Assert that the second gets `brk_b_2`, in sorted order. If the score language rejects that alias, say so in a comment and construct the collision another way.
3. **Missing rule tests:**
   - `samples ../elsewhere` from folder `examples` → catalog_path `elsewhere/x.wav` (not under samples/, so it stays unresolved as-is);
   - `samples ../../x` escaping the root → `../x/…`.
4. **Bug: `sliceName` is lost when the slice is unresolved.** `planScoreRefs` only sets `sliceName` inside the resolved branch. The record must keep `sliceName: ref.sliceName` whenever the score names a slice (the clip or slice is missing, or the slice was renamed), so "which scores name loop-1" still works. Add a test.
5. **Bug: `hasScoreRefChanged` uses `|| 0` / `|| ""`,** so a slice at `start: 0` equals "no slice". Compare with `?? null`.
6. **saveScore writes the Score up to three times.** Parse first (extractReferences), then do **one** upsert of the Score with `text` and `lastErrors` (the messages, or `[]`). Then, only on success, do the ref plan and apply. Drop the final extra update.
7. **Tidy-ups:**
   - the sort becomes `a.alias.cmp(&b.alias).then_with(|| a.kit_pad.cmp(&b.kit_pad)).then_with(|| a.slice_name.cmp(&b.slice_name)).then_with(|| a.source.cmp(&b.source))` (Option already orders None before Some);
   - remove the unused `_base_dir` parameter;
   - in `resolve_catalog_path`, compute `samples_dir` only in the rule (c) branch.

Verification: the spec's block again. Paste the outputs, then ready-for-review.

Review round 2 (storage-lead): everything is accepted except **one test**. Re-run by me: cargo 31 ✓, wasm (5 deepEqual) ✓, tsc ✓, tsx 15/15 ✓, build ✓.

`test_samples_escape_root` doesn't escape the root: `examples/nested/deep` + `../../..` lands exactly at the root, so it asserts `marine-band/x.wav`, which looks like a catalog path, and the comments contradict themselves. Replace it with a real escape: folder `examples`, `samples ../../x` → `catalog_path == Some("../x/marine-band/x.wav")`. Keep the leading `..`; normalize must not drop it. If normalize loses the `..`, fix normalize. Run `cargo test -p apricitus-data`, paste the output, then ready-for-review.
